title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Undertakings
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: During a settlement meeting, a paralegal gives a personal undertaking to opposing counsel that they will forward a specific banking record by Friday at 5:00 PM. On Thursday, the client instructs the paralegal not to send the record. What must the paralegal do?
options: Follow the client's instructions because the paralegal-client relationship is paramount.
Fulfill the undertaking and send the document, as a personal undertaking is an absolute ethical commitment by the paralegal.
Wait until Monday to send the document so the client has time to cool off.
Bill the client for the time spent arguing about the document and then withdraw.
questions.explain: Rule 2.02 (Undertakings): A paralegal must strictly fulfill all undertakings given and honor all trust conditions. A personal undertaking made by a legal professional is binding upon them personally. Because it is binding, the paralegal cannot use the client's subsequent change of heart as an excuse to break the undertaking.

questions.q: During discoveries, a paralegal states on the record: "I undertake to provide the defendant's bank statements by next Friday." However, the paralegal knows obtaining them might be difficult and relies on the client to provide them. If the client fails to provide them, is the paralegal liable?
options: No, an undertaking on behalf of a client does not bind the paralegal personally.
Yes, an undertaking given by a paralegal is a personal ethical commitment; if they cannot control the outcome, they should only promise "best efforts."
No, the tribunal will simply order the client to produce them, releasing the paralegal.
Yes, but the paralegal can unilaterally cancel the undertaking if it becomes too expensive.
questions.explain: Rule 2.02 (Undertakings). An undertaking given by a legal practitioner binds them personally and they must strictly fulfill it. A paralegal should not give an absolute undertaking for something outside of their direct control. If they rely on the client, they should only undertake to use "best efforts" to obtain the documents.
